origin.known_result: Relative anthropogenic resource expansion is nearly unrelated to LepTraits host-family breadth.

mechanistic_question: Why can taxonomic host specialists and generalists gain similar proportional geographic resource opportunity from anthropogenic host redistribution?

fresh_exploratory_hypothesis.statement: Added geographic resource opportunity is often dominated by one or a few disproportionately redistributed host species, so taxonomic host-family breadth is a poor proxy for anthropogenic geographic opportunity.

panel.source: Exact 239-species S1 resource-eligible panel from the aggregate result

host_level_decomposition.native_host_units: For each resolved host species h, WCVP v13 WGSRPD3 units with introduced=0, extinct=0, location_doubtful=0.
host_level_decomposition.contemporary_host_units: For each resolved host species h, WCVP v13 WGSRPD3 units with extinct=0 and location_doubtful=0, retaining native and introduced ranges.
host_level_decomposition.butterfly_added_union: contemporary butterfly host-resource union minus native butterfly host-resource union

fractional_credit_rule.unit_level: For each butterfly-added WGSRPD3 unit, identify all larval host species whose host_added_units include that unit. Split one unit of credit equally among those contributing host species.
fractional_credit_rule.reason: Fractional credit makes total host contribution sum exactly to butterfly-added union size even when introduced host ranges overlap.

primary_descriptive_mechanism.summary: Distribution and median of maximum_single_host_fractional_share among species with introduced_added_units > 0.
primary_descriptive_mechanism.interpretation: High values indicate that anthropogenic opportunity expansion is bottlenecked through a small number of globalized host species.

host_breadth_associations: host-breadth-stratum medians for all contribution metrics
